PMID 11911755 resolves; quote verbatim (conclusion). Same rests on drafter juxtaposition with Grantham 1997 (not re-opened by me); VMAC never mentions dogs. Holds only if comparison_stated:false is allowed; drafter concedes the dog PCWP result post-dates Yoshimura 1991.

Quote verbatim; registry results-first-posted 2012-05-10 confirmed. ASCEND-HF tested dyspnea, death/rehospitalisation and >25% eGFR-fall rate, none a dog-modelled endpoint, so nothing was contradicted. Keep 2002 same (outcomes never modelled); adjudicate the renal claim on ROSE-AHF 2013 instead.

entries.note: Quote verbatim in abstract; untested holds.

PMID 15781736 resolves, PubMed type Meta-Analysis; quote verbatim. Pooled RR 1.52 exists only here, so it is the primary source for that estimate, not a pointer review. Contra holds if meta-analyses satisfy rule 1 (rule_questions 4); model side is drafter juxtaposition.

Quote verbatim; registry date confirmed. Dog hypotension verified in Chen 2009 abstract (systemic BNP gave 'a significant decrease in mean arterial pressure'). Same holds; the contra-to-same reversal and the juxtaposed comparison are rule questions 1 and 5.

missing: efficacy 2013: ROSE-AHF, Chen HH et al. JAMA 2013;310:2533-43, https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2013.282190 (PMID 24247300, PMC3934929; NCT01132846, results posted, first-posted date not retrieved). Low-dose nesiritide 0.005 ug/kg/min in AHF with renal dysfunction: no effect on 72-h urine volume or cystatin C. Direct patient test of the dog decongestion/renal prediction by the Mayo group that ran the dog studies. Status is contra if the prediction is Chen 2004 high-dose renal enhancement, same if it is Chen 2009 (clinical-dose BNP in overt-HF dogs gave only a trend in natriuresis/GFR) or Riegger 1988 (renal effects absent).

safety/efficacy 2004: Wang DJ et al., Circulation 2004, 'Nesiritide does not improve renal function in patients with chronic heart failure and worsening serum creatinine' (crossover RCT). A single primary trial that would date the renal comparison to 2004 and sidestep the meta-analysis question. DOI NOT resolved within budget (PubMed parsed 'does not' as NOT); verify before use.

engagement 1991: Yoshimura 1991, https://doi.org/10.1161/01.cir.84.4.1581 (already cited in the draft's efficacy judgement), reported plasma cGMP rise with BNP infusion in HF patients. Under the draft's own juxtaposition rule this moves engagement to same in 1991, not 2009. Not re-opened by me.
model_filed: nesiritide FDA pharmacology review (NDA 20-920, 2001) would settle whether the pacing-dog model was the filed model; not checked.
rule_questions: 1. Juxtaposition: rule 1 says the primary source must 'make the comparison', but v2's comparison_stated:false presumes drafter juxtaposition is allowed. Four of the six non-untested entries (efficacy 2002 and 2011, safety 2005 and 2011) are juxtapositions; under the strict reading all four are untested. Decide once for the atlas.

2. Null on unmodelled endpoints (efficacy 2011): does a clinical-outcome null on endpoints the model never produced count as contra? The contra definition ('predicted wrongly') says no; the ad-amyloid house example (drugs failed -> contra) says yes when the model readout was the efficacy proxy. Here the proxy (PCWP) held in VMAC, so I applied the definition and proposed same.

3. Dose cell with no exposure target (dose 2009): the dog never issued an exposure/occupancy target and the human dose came from human escalation. Is the source's stated BP match a dose comparison (same), or is the cell untested? I proposed untested; either excludes contra because the only published comparison calls the canine predictive.

4. Meta-analysis as primary source (safety 2005): rule 1 excludes 'reviews' but a meta-analysis generates the estimate being cited. I treated it as satisfying rule 1. If not, safety 2005 becomes untested and the renal signal is first dated by Wang 2004 (unverified) or by ASCEND-HF 2011 (refuted).

5. Status reversal: 'contra overrides every matched status' - per entry/year, or permanent? Safety moves contra (2005) -> same (2011) on a 7,141-patient trial that refuted the earlier signal. I read the rule as per time point.
6. Unchanged-status entries: engagement 2018 repeats same only to record a subjects change (volunteers -> patients); the brief says one entry per change of status.

7. Which dog paper is 'the prediction' for the renal claim: high-dose Chen 2004 (GFR enhancement) versus clinical-dose Chen 2009 and Riegger 1988 (renal resistance, effects absent). The renal-axis statuses in efficacy and safety flip on this choice; the brief's 'model the class relied on' does not pick between papers from the same lab.
